findings.quote: Raymond Svider, associated with the controlling holder BC Partners, serves as Chairperson, so the chair and chief-executive roles are separated.
findings.issue: The proxy excerpt in Context establishes only that 'Mr. Svider serves as Chairperson.' It does not state that Svider is associated with, or an executive of, BC Partners. The only director-to-Argos affiliation the proxy carries is Mr. Star's, via Longview's minority interest in Argos Holdings. Tying Svider to BC Partners is a recalled-executive affiliation, and governance claims must rest on the proxy that is captured.
findings.fix: Say Svider serves as Chairperson and Singh as CEO, that the roles are separated (all supported), and drop 'associated with the controlling holder BC Partners' unless the proxy excerpt is expanded to carry that affiliation.
findings.note: Rewrite now reads 'Raymond Svider serves as Chairperson, so the chair and chief-executive roles are separated.' The unsupported BC Partners affiliation is removed; not reintroduced elsewhere.

findings.quote: SmartPak adds equine and Modern Animal adds veterinary care, broadening the offering beyond core retail.
findings.issue: The surface names the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions (press release, MD&A active-customer footnotes) but never says what either business is. Attributing equine to SmartPak and veterinary care to Modern Animal is a recalled characterization the pack does not support. The same unsupported tie recurs in sections.businessMoat.moatFactors[2] ('extended by ... the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions') and sections.growth.points[2] ('The SmartPak equine and Modern Animal veterinary acquisitions').
findings.fix: Refer to the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions without asserting their categories, or describe the expansion using the grounded categories the MD&A lists (equine specialty products; veterinary clinic services) without pinning each to a named deal.
findings.note: catalysts[3] now 'the SmartPak and Modern Animal deals broaden the platform and contributed customers in the quarter'; growth.points[2] 'extend the platform into adjacent pet categories and services'; moatFactors[2] no longer ties equine/veterinary to either deal. All unsupported category ties removed.

findings.quote: Growth maturity: net sales grew 5.7% excluding acquisitions and active customers rose 3.8% to 21.7 million, so the top line depends increasingly on spending more per customer and on acquired businesses.
findings.issue: The idiosyncratic risks restate the executive-summary risk pointers almost verbatim rather than arguing behind them. idiosyncratic[0] repeats exec risks[0] (5.7% ex-acquisitions and 3.8% to 21.7M); idiosyncratic[1] repeats exec risks[1] ($85.9M share-based compensation added back to the forward multiple); idiosyncratic[2] repeats exec risks[2] (BC Partners' 88.4% voting control limiting minority influence). The house rule is that exec-summary risks point and the sections argue; each figure's story is told once.
findings.fix: Make the exec-summary risks one-line pointers and let risks.idiosyncratic carry the mechanism and what-to-watch, so the 5.7%/3.8%/21.7M, the $85.9M SBC and the 88.4% control figures each appear once with the argument in the section, not twice with the same figures.
findings.note: Exec-summary risks are now figure-free pointers ('organic sales and active-customer gains have decelerated'; adjusted-earnings quality; controlled company; competition), while risks.idiosyncratic keeps the 5.7%/3.8%/21.7M, $85.9M SBC and 88.4% figures once with the argument. Point-then-argue split restored.

findings.quote: Autoship's rising share of sales, up to 84.6% from 83.0% a year earlier, shifts the mix toward recurring, higher-retention revenue.
findings.issue: Several figures are retold across sections in different words. Autoship 84.6% vs 83.0% (and 9.3% to $2,817.2M) appears in catalysts[1], businessMoat.segments and growth.points[0]. The raised full-year outlook appears in catalysts[0] and growth.points[1]. Net sales per active customer of $602 appears in businessMoat.segments and growth.points[4]. The probability-weighted fair value ~$24 / expected upside ~32% / reward-risk ~1.28x triple appears in analystCommentary, valuation.scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[0]. Rubric item 7: introduce each figure once per section and refer back in words.
findings.fix: Keep each figure in the one section that argues it and refer back in words elsewhere: cite the Autoship mix once (moat), the outlook once, $602 once, and the E/upside/reward-risk numbers once (scenario commentary), letting the summary and final recommendation point to them rather than re-quote them.
findings.note: growth.points[0] and [4] now carry no Autoship 84.6%/83.0% or $602 figures; the raised outlook is no longer repeated in growth; the E/upside/reward-risk triple was removed from thesis and finalRecommendation, leaving it in the header commentary plus the one scenario section that argues it. Each figure now sits in a summary pointer plus a single arguing section.

findings.quote: Chewy's demand is tied to consumer discretionary spending on pets, which the 10-K notes is sensitive to inflation, interest rates and broader economic uncertainty.
findings.issue: The 'inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates, and broader economic uncertainty' language is from the 10-Q MD&A 'Macroeconomic Considerations' section, not the 10-K. The 10-K risk factor on the surface reads 'Uncertainties in economic conditions, industry trends, and market conditions, and their impact on the pet market.' Attributing the specific triad to 'the 10-K' misnames the source within the pack.
findings.fix: Attribute the inflation/interest-rate/uncertainty phrasing to the 10-Q's MD&A, or reword to the 10-K's own economic-conditions risk-factor language if the 10-K is to be cited.
findings.note: Now reads 'which the company's quarterly MD&A notes is sensitive to inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates and broader economic uncertainty' — attribution corrected to the 10-Q MD&A, matching the source that carries the phrasing.

findings.quote: Intense e-commerce competition from larger general retailers with greater scale and resources.
findings.issue: The 10-K risk factor on the surface says internet-based competition is strong, but the surface does not establish that competitors are 'larger general retailers with greater scale and resources.' The scale/resources characterization is not grounded (it recurs in businessMoat.moatFactors[3] and risks.systemic). No specific peer is named, so this is a mild embellishment rather than an ungrounded-peer violation.
findings.fix: Frame competition using the grounded language ('strong, especially Internet-based competition' per the 10-K) and drop the unsupported claim that competitors have greater scale and resources.
findings.note: exec risks[4] now 'Strong internet-based competition in pet retail limits pricing power'; moatFactors[3] and risks.systemic likewise drop 'greater scale and resources'. Competition is now framed in the 10-K's own grounded language.
